summary: The greedy scan reads each character once, matching the worst-case input-inspection lower bound; the fixed 26-letter alphabet also prevents the natural partition DP from defining a genuinely slower scalable class.

optimality.argument: Changing an unread late character can introduce or remove a forced duplicate boundary and alter the answer, so every character may need inspection. The accepted scan performs a constant number of bit operations per character and therefore matches this lower bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: An adversary can change an unread character to duplicate a letter in the current part or avoid that duplicate, changing the minimum partition count.
The greedy reference processes each character once and stores only a 26-bit used-letter mask.
Regression exhaustively compares all strings over a three-letter alphabet through length eight and deterministic long strings against an independent partition dynamic program.
